summary: Backend-only verification for the Reels page bug fix (pagingEnabled restored + iOS autoplay-safe player init). All 6 new iteration-8 tests PASS and the full 43-test iteration 6/7 regression suite (test_iteration6_regression.py + test_purge_verify.py + test_push_pipeline.py + test_push_edge_cases.py) still PASS — 49/49 green in 15.3s. Confirmed: (1) GET /api/reels returns the 1 seeded reel owned by semidiepie with valid id/type=reel/video_url/author.id/likes/comments_count. (2) video_url (Cloudinary MP4) HEAD → 200, content-type video/mp4;codecs=hvc1. (3) POST /api/posts/{id}/like → 200 and likes increments by 1 with liked_by_me=true (authenticated GET). (4) DELETE /api/posts/{id}/like → 200 and likes decrements with liked_by_me=false. (5) POST /api/posts/{id}/comments {"text":"…"} → 200 and the comment is visible in GET /api/posts/{id}/comments. (6) Expo bundler at http://localhost:3000 returns HTTP 200 with PostMePlex HTML — the FlatList config change bundles cleanly (no metro errors in expo.err.log). True TikTok-style paging + iOS autoplay of the <VideoView> is a native primitive and cannot be exercised from web preview / curl; that requires a physical iOS/Android device. Code inspection of /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/reels.tsx confirms the described fixes are actually applied: pagingEnabled prop present (line 312), snapToInterval removed, explicit style={{height: reelHeight}} removed from the FlatList, initialNumToRender=1 / maxToRenderPerBatch=2 / windowSize=3 / removeClippedSubviews={Platform.OS === 'android'} present, and the useVideoPlayer initializer sets p.muted=true and calls p.play() (lines 47-53), then the active-index effect flips muted=false and calls play() again (lines 60-61).
critical_code_review_comments: reels.tsx fix looks correct: pagingEnabled is the right primitive for TikTok-style full-viewport paging when itemHeight == viewportHeight — snapToInterval alone is known to be flaky on native and dropping it is the right call.
Initializing the useVideoPlayer with muted=true + play() sidesteps iOS's user-gesture autoplay restriction, then unmuting on activeIndex change is a clean pattern.
Minor: server.py is still 1921 lines — recommend splitting into routers/services in a future iteration (>700 line threshold). Not a blocker.

seed_data_creation: One TEST_-prefixed comment added to the seeded reel by test_comment_create_and_list. Will not be purged (comment purge only cascades from purged users, not by text prefix) — negligible and does not affect subsequent runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend at port 8001 via supervisor, EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in frontend/.env. Founder: semidiepie@gmail.com / Semi123!. The reel likes counter is idempotent per (user, post): POSTing /like twice does NOT double-count and does not error either — always normalise state to unliked before asserting increments, and always pass Authorization to GET /api/reels when you need the accurate liked_by_me flag (unauth GET always returns liked_by_me=false). Reel author is at `author.id`/`author.username`, not top-level `author_id`. True Reels page playback + vertical paging can only be verified on a physical iOS/Android device — not on Expo web preview.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: pagingEnabled had been dropped in the prior UI iteration, so vertical scroll relied on snapToInterval alone which is unreliable when item height == viewport height; and the video player was created with muted=false without calling play() up-front, so iOS's autoplay-without-user-gesture policy blocked the first render. Fix applied by main agent restores pagingEnabled, removes the redundant snapToInterval + height style, and initialises the player muted+playing (unmuting only when the reel is the active one). Backend contract is unchanged — this iteration is purely a frontend RN primitive fix and a regression-only backend run confirms nothing broke server-side.
